As some of you know, I am a professional pterosaur hunter. What does that mean? Well, I'll explain. Pterosaurs were flying reptiles that lived around the time of the dinosaurs. They are avemetatarsalians just like their closest relatives-the dinosaurs. They ruled the skies from 228 million years ago to 65 million years ago when the meteor that killed the non-avian dinosaurs, plesiosaurs, mosasaurs, and pterosaurs struck. Or so we think. While non-avian dinosaurs, plesiosaurs, and mosasaurs are clearly extinct-some animals-like pterosaurs actually survived. The pterosaurs that survived were pterodactyloid pterosaurs (other pterosaurs types like dimorphodons and Rhamphorhynchids were already extinct by the Jurassic). However these pterodactyloid pterosaurs were different from the majority of pterosaurs. They were generally MUCH smaller and very few ended up regaining their position as large flying animals (a notable exception would be the Ropen). Now these pterosaurs are INCREDIBLY rare (that is why so few people have seen them) the VAST majority of flying niches were taken by the birds seeing as more birds survived the KT extinction than pterosaurs. Now you may be asking where is the proof for all of this? Well up until now the only proof we had were the rare sighting of pterosaur that most people just assumed were birds. Most people can't imagine that pterosaurs could have survived the KT especially since there are no fossils after the KT. The reason there are no fossils of post-KT pterosaurs is because their bones are incredibly fragile and don't fossilize well. We even have a hard time finding Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous era fossils of pterosaurs because their bones do not fossilize well. It is similar to the coelecanth. It also has bones that do not fossilize well. They also (like modern pterosaurs) live in very secluded areas of the world where they are VERY difficult to find. Now what I am about to show you is a solid piece of proof that pterosaurs still live to this day. On a trip to Costa Rica, I went looking for pterosaurs. There is one type of pterosaur that lives DEEP in the Costa Rican jungles and rarely leaves the canopy. In fact, in all likelyhood burrow for the majority of the year.
